metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full (transcript-derived, code-verified — no live irrlichd observation yet); driver_capability: ready (send/wait_turn/exit_clean live-proven end-to-end in commit 0239a1bd)

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

### agent_supports: yes

Muse's interactive TUI (bare `muse`, no subcommand) runs a normal single-prompt round trip: the user sends one line, the model replies, control returns to the composer. This is the smallest unit muse's own session model supports — one `runtime.session`/`kind:"run"` stream per prompt, opened by `event.kind:"started"` (carries the literal prompt) and closed by `event.kind:"terminal"` (`muse-format-spec.md` §3, 37 terminal samples across a 14-session corpus: 31 `completed`, 5 `cancelled`, 1 `failed`). A reply-only turn with no tool use is exactly the `completed`/no-tool-calls case, the modal outcome in that sample (31/37).

### daemon_capability: full

The adapter (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/agent.go`) declares `Source = agent.FilesUnderRoot{Dir: defaultRootDir, ..., Parser: JSONLineParser{muse.Parser}}` — a plain transcript-tree adapter, single session id from the session directory (`~/.local/share/muse/sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/<uuid>/session.jsonl`), no hooks (Permissions carries one `transcripts` observe-only key; the package doc on `Agent()` states the research found no native hook/callback mechanism). Walking the scenario's two user-observable signals against `parser.go` as it exists today:

1. **`ready → working → ready`.** `parseRunStarted` (parser.go:308-315) sets `EventType="user_message"` + `ClearToolNames=true` on `event.kind:"started"` — the SessionDetector force-bounces ready→working on fresh activity the same way every no-hooks adapter does. `parseRunTerminal` (parser.go:324-365) sets `EventType="turn_done"` unconditionally on `event.kind:"terminal"` for ALL three outcomes (`completed`/`cancelled`/`failed`) — the turn objectively ended in every case; only the `failed` branch additionally sets `SessionError` so the classifier routes to `error` instead of `ready` (`state_classifier.go`'s `classifyAgentDone`, per `muse-adapter-contract.md` §5). For the happy-path recipe (a text-only reply, no tool call, no error), `LastEventType=="turn_done"` with no open tool call and no `SessionError` drives `IsAgentDone()`→`ready` exactly as `session.go`'s `IsAgentDone` (metrics.go:562-608) requires. `parser_test.go` pins this directly: `TestParseLine_RunTerminal_*` (lines ~105,125,163) assert `EventType=="turn_done"` for completed/cancelled/failed, and a metrics-level test (lines 598-605) asserts `m.LastEventType=="turn_done"` with nonzero cumulative tokens after a full completed-turn fixture (`testdata/real-turn-completed.jsonl`, a real redacted capture).
2. **`TotalTokens > 0` after the turn.** `parseModelCompleted` (parser.go:371-422) reads `event.kind:"model_completed"`'s `usage` object (input/output/cache_read/cache_write) and sets `ev.Tokens` whenever `Input>0 || Output>0`, feeding `tailer_metrics.go`'s cumulative-token accumulation the same way every other adapter's per-call usage event does. `parser_test.go` (line ~198) pins `ev.Tokens.Input`/`.Output` off a real `model_completed` fixture record.

Both spec-required observables are emitted correctly by the parser as read today, so daemon=full — not a narrower `bug`/`incapable`. `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` passes (`ok irrlicht/core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse 1.226s`, run directly for this assessment).

### driver_capability: ready

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"` — every step type this recipe needs (`send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`, `exit_clean`) is implemented, not stubbed. Commit `0239a1bd` ("fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass", same day as this assessment) fixed five live-reproduced defects that would otherwise have broken exactly this recipe (untrusted-workspace modal eating the first `send`, a dropped Enter keystroke, `resolve_transcript` resolving into a subagent's transcript instead of the driven session's own, a silent `tmux kill-session` teardown instead of a real `session.end` record, and `turn_count()` silently swallowing a read failure as "zero turns") plus a sixth found while live-proving the fix (a startup race that dropped the first `send` before muse's input handler was wired up). The commit message states the fix was "proven live against muse 1.2.1 via tmux, including one full send -> wait_turn -> exit_clean run through the actual driver that... counts the turn correctly, and leaves a real session.end(exit_reason: clean) record on disk" — i.e. exactly this scenario's step sequence, live-verified end to end.

## What is still provisional

The daemon verdict above is grounded in the parser's code + its unit tests against real (redacted) transcript fixtures, and in the driver's own live-proof of producing a correct transcript — but neither of those routes the resulting transcript through a live `irrlichd` and reads its `events.jsonl`/session state back. Whether the SessionDetector's timing (poll cadence, ready-birth vs working-birth at discovery) behaves as the code implies for a session.jsonl that already carries early bookkeeping records (`route_facts`, `metadata`, the permission-profile `retained_frame`, all Skip=true) before the first `started` event is UNVERIFIED by an actual recording — this is exactly what `record` is for, and confidence is held at 0.8 (not ≥0.9) for that reason.
caveats: Vacuous-pass check: this cell would pass while proving nothing if the recipe's reply somehow triggered a tool call the phase spec doesn't check for, or if `record` reused a stale/replay-golden fixture instead of a fresh live capture. Mitigated by adding an explicit no-tool-call invariant to the spec (see expected.jsonl) and by the routing table requiring a real `record` pass, not an assess-only pass, before the cell shows as observed.

Load-bearing environment precondition: the recipe's launch flag `--trust-workspace` is required for every run because `$RUN_CWD` is always a brand-new directory (muse-driver-audit.md, live-reproduced: a bare `muse` launch against a fresh cwd fires an untrusted-workspace modal that silently eats the first `send`). This is a driver-side mitigation, not an environment property that varies by machine, so it is baked into the driver rather than listed as a host-specific prerequisite.

model is intentionally NOT pinned in observations. A live capture during the driver audit (muse-driver-audit.md, defect #1 evidence) showed the TUI banner reading 'Model set to muse-spark-1.3-contributor' for a fresh session on this machine, but 'contributor' reads as an account/tier-scoped default rather than a documented, stable default — pinning it risks failing every future recording's verify on an account-dependent string (the same 'don't hard-pin a doc-guessed model' concern the assess playbook calls out for doc-derived names, extended here to a single ad hoc live observation). Left provisional for `record` to fill from the actual recording.

cost_nonzero is asserted false, not true. `core/pkg/capacity/remote.go` sources all model pricing from BerriAI/litellm's public `model_prices_and_context_window.json`; `core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go` has no entry for 'muse', 'spark', or any Meta-internal model family, and `tailer.NormalizeModelName` (core/pkg/tailer/parser.go:942) only rewrites a handful of Claude aliases — 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor' passes through unchanged and, per `TestModelAliases_UnknownReturnsUnchanged`, an unrecognized model name prices at exactly $0 (ContextWindow=0, Pricing=nil). This is a general pricing-catalog gap for any unpriced/proprietary model, not a muse-specific daemon defect, so it stays a caveat rather than downgrading daemon_capability.

Session-birth timing (session_birth/pid_bind max_delay_ms in expected.jsonl) is an estimate, not a live measurement: format-spec evidence (`route_facts`/`.session.lock` both written at session start, before any prompt) supports a single-birth-into-ready shape like claudecode/aider/junie rather than copilot/mistral-vibe's presession split, but no live irrlichd recording has yet measured the actual latency between tmux launch and the session directory becoming visible to FilesUnderRoot's watcher. `record` should tighten or loosen these bounds from the real recording.

§5 — the exact classifier ladder (IsAgentDone, LastEventType==turn_done, classifyAgentDone) a no-hooks adapter like muse must satisfy, and what ParseLine sets
Live-reproduced defects #1-#5 in the interactive driver, all now fixed; workspace-trust modal evidence backing the --trust-workspace caveat
parseRunStarted (turn open, user_message), parseRunTerminal (turn close, turn_done for all 3 terminal outcomes), parseModelCompleted (token accounting)
TestParseLine_RunTerminal_* (turn_done pinned for completed/cancelled/failed), token-snapshot test against a real model_completed fixture, metrics-level cumulative-token test
Source = FilesUnderRoot (single-birth transcript-tree Source), one observe-only 'transcripts' permission, no hooks
CanonicalStates/IsAgentDone — LastEventType==turn_done is the no-hooks authoritative end-of-turn signal
DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean" — every primitive this recipe needs is implemented, not stubbed
liteLLMURL = BerriAI/litellm's model_prices_and_context_window.json — the sole pricing source
grep for 'muse'/'spark' returns nothing — no alias maps muse's model id onto a priced entry
TestModelAliases_UnknownReturnsUnchanged — an unrecognized model prices at exactly $0 (ContextWindow=0, Pricing=nil)
Commit fixing all 5 driver-audit defects + a 6th startup-race defect found while live-proving the fix; states the full send->wait_turn->exit_clean sequence was live-verified against muse 1.2.1
Run directly for this assessment: ok, 1.226s

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1 per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
muse auth complete: 'muse login' (Meta account, browser code approval) or META_API_KEY exported — auth is set up out-of-band, the rig's precheck delegates it to the user
tmux available — the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL so it stays alive across the turn (bare `muse` with no subcommand starts the interactive TUI)
irrlichd is recording — either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record
setup: The interactive driver (driver-interactive.sh) creates a fresh empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and launches `muse --trust-workspace` in a tmux session there, then sleeps 1s for muse's own input handler to wire up before the first send (both live-reproduced necessities per muse-driver-audit.md defects #1 and the startup-race follow-up)
--trust-workspace is REQUIRED, not optional: every staging cwd is brand-new, so muse's 'Do you trust this workspace?' modal fires on every run and silently eats the first prompt without it

muse mints its own session UUID on launch; the driver resolves the newest session.jsonl under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions (excluding subagent/ copies) newer than a pre-launch marker once the turn completes

The send is a no-tool single turn — muse is asked to reply with exactly one word, so the working span carries no tool call (tool_calls_max: 0) and the session never enters waiting (no approval prompt fires)

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl mints the session in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishes launching (single-birth; session id from the session directory basename == stream.id)
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event binding the muse-bin PID to the session (via .session.lock's held flock fd, per pid.go)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working when the user prompt lands (event.kind:"started" -> user_message)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to ready after the text-only assistant reply (event.kind:"terminal",terminal:"completed" -> turn_done)
no state_transition to waiting occurs, and no function_call/tool-call event occurs (no tool use in a one-word reply)
final session state is ready before exit_clean tears the REPL down
the turn's cumulative TotalTokens > 0 (from model_completed's usage object)
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=true, cost_nonzero=false (model is unpriced in the litellm catalog), model unpinned
